author: Blum, T. and others
title: Domain wall QCD with physical quark masses
abstract: We present results for several light hadronic quantities ($f_\pi$, $f_K$, $B_K$, $m_{ud}$, $m_s$, $t_0^{1/2}$, $w_0$) obtained from simulations of 2+1 flavor domain wall lattice QCD with large physical volumes and nearly-physical pion masses at two lattice spacings. We perform a short, $\mathcal{O}(3)\%$, extrapolation in pion mass to the physical values by combining our new data in a simultaneous chiral/continuum 'global fit' with a number of other ensembles with heavier pion masses. We use the physical values of $m_\pi$, $m_K$ and $m_\Omega$ to determine the two quark masses and the scale - all other quantities are outputs from our simulations. We obtain results with sub-percent statistical errors and negligible chiral and finite-volume systematics for these light hadronic quantities, including: $f_\pi = 130.2(9)$ MeV; $f_K = 155.5(8)$ MeV; the average up/down quark mass and strange quark mass in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme at 3 GeV, $2.997(49)$ and $81.64(1.17)$ MeV respectively; and the neutral kaon mixing parameter, $B_K$, in the RGI scheme, $0.750(15)$ and the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme at 3 GeV, $0.530(11)$.

data.note: The quoted errors are statistical; the paper states that chiral-extrapolation and finite-volume systematics are negligible for these quantities.

Quark masses are MSbar masses at 3 GeV. The second error is the paper's perturbative-truncation error from matching the intermediate RI-SMOM scheme to MSbar; no separate chiral or finite-volume systematic is quoted. The ms/mud ratio carries only a statistical error because the matching error cancels.

BK is the MSbar value at 3 GeV; BhatK is the renormalization-group-invariant value. The second error is the paper's perturbative-truncation error, estimated as the difference between the two RI-SMOM intermediate schemes.
